A simple diagram showing how a syllable splits into onset and rhyme. Three rows for the words "cat", "hat" and "flat". Each word is drawn as a long rounded bar split into two coloured blocks: a pale blue block on the left for the onset (/k/, /h/, /fl/) and a soft orange block on the right for the rhyme (/æt/). The three orange blocks line up vertically to show that they are identical, with a curved bracket on the right joining them. Clean flat educational illustration, white background, soft colours.

A three-circle Venn-style chart comparing homophones, homographs and homonyms. Left circle (soft blue) titled "Homophones – same sound" with the examples "sea / see" and "right / write". Right circle (soft green) titled "Homographs – same spelling" with the example "lead (to guide) / lead (metal)" and "tear (from the eye) / tear (to rip)". The overlap of the two circles (soft yellow) titled "Homonyms – same sound AND same spelling" with the examples "bank (money) / bank (river)" and "bat (animal) / bat (sport)". Small icons: an ear for sound, a pencil for spelling. Clean flat educational illustration, white background.
